Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The Australian fielders are out in the middle. Evin Lewis and Shimron Hetmyer walk out to bat. Mitchell Starc will start with the ball. Here we go..

Right then! 252 is what Australia have scored. The DLS revised target for West Indies will be 257, the pitch isn't the easiest to bat on so it will be interesting to see how they approach it. Do join us for the chase as it shall start in a short while.

Ashton Turner says that the conditions are really foreign to use but we are getting used to them due to the T20 series. Adds that the spinners will enjoy bowling here. Says that Alex and he got out at the wrong time but they still have a decent score. Further adds that the wicket will help the bowlers and they should look to take advantage of that.

West Indies did not have the best of starts with the ball as Sheldon Cottrell and Jason Holder struggled to find their rhythm at the start. But in the middle overs, Akeal Hosein and Alzarri Joseph rocked the Australian top order with two wickets each. There was a strong stand in the middle overs and Aussies seemed well set to put on a massive score but Hayden Walsh dismissed both the set batters in the same over and went on to take his first 5-wicket haul in ODIs to make sure that the Australian tail doesn't wag much. He also became the first West Indian spinner to take 5-fer in ODIs since 2016.

Australia had a decent start as Josh Philippe and Ben McDermott put on a 50-run stand. Josh Philippe fell after getting a start of 39 runs and the same happened with Mitchell Marsh as he fell for 20. Moises Henriques struggled for a while before getting out while looking to sweep and Ben McDermott fell soon after. They were staring down the barrel but a brilliant stand between the skipper, Alex Carey, and Ashton Turner led the recovery. They put on a 100-run stand, Carey scored a fifty while Turner stayed on 49. There were three rain stoppages in between but the batters didn't seem to be too affected by them and carried on with their work. Carey and Turner fell in the same over in the death and their lower order imploded as they ended up scoring 252 in 49 overs.

A good bowling performance by West Indies means that they have restricted Australia to an average score. The Australian batting was all about that one partnership in the middle overs as everyone else struggled to get going on a two-paced pitch.

Drinks break! Australia got a good start with Josh Philippe looking in good touch in the first few overs but his wicket, followed by that of Mitchell Marsh will put them under some pressure. Their middle order isn't the most experienced and West Indies will look to take advantage of just that and pick a few quick wickets. Also, Moises Henriques is the new batter.
Review time! Oh well, Mitchell Marsh is walking already.

At first, the umpire did not give it but the moment West Indies reviewed this, Marsh started walking as he knew that he got some glove on it. Huge wicket this, of the in-form batter Marsh for the West Indies and they are elated.

Flighted ball, on off. Ben McDermott defends it towards point.
BEATEN! Tosses it up, around off. Ben McDermott looks to defend on the back foot, but is beaten on the outside edge as the ball turns away just enough.
A short leg comes in now.
Tossed up, around off. Josh Philippe sweeps it to deep square leg for one.
Tossed up on leg stump. Josh Philippe defends it off the back foot.
First change of the game! Akeal Hosein comes in the attack now.
Short of a length, on off. Ben McDermott defends it off the back foot with ease.
Fuller ball, on middle. Ben McDermott takes a step down the track and tucks it to the leg side.
Serves a length ball, around off. Blocked out with ease.
FOUR! Just past! Short ball, outside off. Ben McDermott cuts it past the diving cover fielder and gets the boundary.
Serves a length ball, on the sixth stump line. Left alone now.
Short and wide now. Ben McDermott cuts it past covers for a couple of runs.
FOUR! Punished! Short ball, on the body. Sheldon Cottrell isn't bowling at an express pace so Josh Philippe has no qualms in pulling this to the square leg fence.
Good length ball, around off. Josh Philippe clips it to square leg.
Back of a length, on off. Punched to the right of mid on for a couple.
Full and wide now. Josh Philippe drives it past covers for a couple of runs.

SIX! Picked up! He seems to be very confident in playing the short ball. Well, this isn't the deadliest of short balls to be fair. A nice short one, down the leg side. Josh Philippe swivels and pulls it just over the fine leg fence.
Josh Philippe nails the off drive but straight to mid off.
Length ball, around off. Ben McDermott blocks this one solidly.
Back of a length ball, around off. Josh Philippe taps it towards point for a quick single and the slight fumble allows with it ease.
Good length ball outside off. Punches towards covers by Josh Philippe.
Back of a length ball, pushed towards mid off.
Length ball, around off. Turned towards point.
Short and wide. Ben McDermott drags it to mid off for one. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses.
Short ball, on leg stump. Josh Philippe pulls it straight to the short fine leg fielder. A few yards to either side would have been four runs for him.
Good length ball, on leg, defended back to the bowler now.
FOUR! Top shot! Short ball around waist high. Josh Philippe pulls it to fine leg for a boundary.
Full ball, on middle. Josh Philippe drives it to the mid on fielder.
Good length ball, on off. Josh Philippe blocks it to the cover fielder.
Short of a good length ball on off. Josh Philippe defends it off the back foot.
Serves a full one, around off. Ben McDermott blocks it out.

Just wide of the fielder! Back of a length, lands on off and moves away a touch. It takes the outside edge and goes past the diving second slip fielder. The man from third man cuts it off and they get a single.
Short of a length, outside off. Josh Philippe cuts it to covers.
Fuller ball, on off. Pushed to covers.
Weather - It is cloudy out there and there are some grey clouds hovering around. The humidity will make it tough for the players.
Good length ball, wide enough for Josh Philippe to leave it.
Back of a length, outside off. Josh Philippe gets the under edge towards the keeper as he looks to cut.
A nice solid front foot defence to end the over here!
Short of a length, on middle. Ben McDermott is a touch late in the pull shot and drags it to square leg.
Serves a fuller ball, around off. Pushed to covers now.
Off the mark in ODIs! Full ball, on the pads. Ben McDermott clips it past square leg for a couple of runs.
Shorter ball, around the ribs. Ben McDermott clips it to the leg side.
Back of a length, around off. Ben McDermott's first ball in ODIs is a solid defence from the crease.
Length ball on off. Defended solidly towards the cover region.
Short and wide. Josh Philippe misses the cut and gets beaten on the outside edge.
Good length ball outside off. Josh Philippe drags it to the mid on fielder.
FOUR! Good shot! Short and wide outside off. Josh Philippe gets on top and punches it past covers for a boundary.
Good length ball outside off. Josh Philippe shoulders arms to this one.
Length ball on off. Blocked towards the mid off fielder.
Who will start from the other end and use the other new ball? Jason Holder it is!
Full ball outside off. Josh Philippe drives it towards mid off for one.
Good length ball on leg stump. Josh Philippe turns it to the short mid-wicket fielder.
Length ball on the pads. Josh Philippe is off the mark as he clips it to fine leg for a couple. A special feeling to get first runs in ODI cricket.
There is a loud appeal for LBW. But the inside edge saves Josh Philippe. He looks to flick this ball but gets the inside edge back on the pads.
WIDE! Sprayed down the leg side. Called Wide.
Full and wide outside off. Josh Philippe lets it through to the keeper.
Starts with a good length ball on the pads. Josh Philippe looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the pads.

We are set to begin! The players take the knee first to protest racial discrimination. Josh Philippe and Ben McDermott, the two debutants will open the batting. Sheldon Cottrell to start with the ball.

Darren Ganga is down for the pitch report, says that the straight boundary is 70 meters in length but the boundaries square of the wicket are smaller. Adds that teams usually like to chase here and there is some even covering of grass on the surface.

Justin Langer, the Australian coach, is down for a chat. Says that he loves being back in Barbados. Adds that it was a tough T20 series but they are getting better now. Says that there are challenges of being in a bio-bubble because you cannot explore the countries where you tour. Further says that they miss the crowds that used to come pre-covid.
Pollard says that he is happy to be back and his body is doing well. Adds that he would have batted first as well but the toss is also 50-50.
Alex Carey says that the wicket looks quite nice. Adds that it is a great privilege to lead the side and he is really excited. Informs that Josh, Ben and Wes will make their debut

West Indies (Playing XI) - Evin Lewis, Darren Bravo, Shimron Hetmyer, Jason Mohammed, Nicholas Pooran (WK), Kieron Pollard (C), Jason Holder, Hayden Walsh, Sheldon Cottrell, Alzarri Joseph, Akeal Hosein.
Australia (Playing XI) - Ben McDermott, Josh Philippe, Mitchell Marsh, Moises Henriques, Alex Carey (C & WK), Ashton Turner, Matthew Wade, Mitchell Starc, Wes Agar, Adam Zampa, Josh Hazlewood.
TOSS - The news from the middle is that Australia have won the toss and they will bat first.

Fun fact - This is Australia's first ODI since they played India back in December 2020 and Alex Carey and Moises Henriques are the only batsmen from that side to be in the squad now. Matthew Wade was not a part of that side but was very much a part of the squad and in all likelihood, should slot in for Finch tonight. To say that a lot depends on these senior folks, would be an understatement.

Australia on the other hand will be led by Alex Carey for the first time as Aaron Finch is ruled out of the 1st ODI due to an injury. It will be interesting to see if Mitchell Marsh brings his red hot form into the ODI series and helps them put on a better fight after a disappointing T20I series. Young and promising Josh Philippe could well be used by Australia at the top of the order in absence of Finch. Australia badly need their batting unit to step up and support their bowlers which they failed to do in the T20 series. It promises to be a cracker of a match. Stay tuned for the toss and the team news.

Hello and welcome to one and all! The action now shifts to the iconic Kensington Oval, Barbados. Another riveting contest awaits us as two strong limited-over sides will go head to head in a three-match ODI series. West Indies led by Kieron Pollard, if he is fit, will be coming into the ODI series high on confidence as they clinched the T20 series quite comfortably. There would be some new faces in the WI squad with the likes of Shai Hope, Roston Chase, Alzarri Joseph, etc.
